title: Fordism
extractedText: Fordism is an industrial engineering and manufacturing system that serves as the basis of modern social and labor-economic systems that support industrialized, standardized mass production and mass consumption. The concept is named after Henry Ford. It is used in social, economic, and management theory about production, working conditions, consumption, and related phenomena, especially regarding the 20th century. Fordism has also been described as a manufacturing system designed to produce standardized, low-cost goods and afford its workers decent enough wages to buy them, and as a model of economic expansion and technological progress based on mass production: the manufacture of standardized products in huge volumes using special-purpose machinery and unskilled labor. Efficiency both decreased the price of cars and allowed Ford to increase his workers' wages, so that common workers could buy their own cars.
